title: Stop-loss and Leverage in optimal Statistical Arbitrage with an application to Energy market

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper develops a statistical arbitrage trading strategy for mean-reverting asset prices modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, incorporating proportional transaction costs, a stop-loss level, and leverage. The investor establishes entry and exit bands around the mean, along with an ex-ante stop-loss level, and rebalances portfolio wealth across a risk-free asset and the risky security in a self-financing repeated strategy. The strategy is evaluated analytically for long-run return via first-exit times and tested empirically on a half-hour energy futures spread dataset (Heating-Oil and Gas-Oil).
extraction.universe: Energy futures pair (Heating Oil second future contract and Gas Oil sixth future contract, HOc2-LGOc6)

key_findings: The introduction of stop-loss and leverage into optimal statistical arbitrage allows analytical derivation of the long-run return based on first-exit times and trading band probabilities for continuous mean-reverting processes.
For an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, expected first-exit times can be expressed explicitly via elementary functions.

Optimal leverage derived analytically is often too large for practical purposes, but empirical application to energy futures shows that the strategy provides significant Out-of-Sample long-run returns even under suboptimal leverage.
limitations: The theoretically derived optimal leverage can be excessively high for practical implementation.
Assumes a constant Ornstein-Uhlenbeck parameter description that may not fully persist in the future, necessitating a stop-loss constraint.
